findings.reason: a §2 node built from §2's own text will not create the constant §8 depends on, so either §2's brief or §8's mechanism must be changed before either is dispatched.
findings.text: §8 says `RUN_DELIVERED_STATUSES` is the constant "which §2's implementation adds", but §2's authored text names no such constant and the §2 implementation in the tree adds none (it adds `AWAITING_UPSTREAM_PHASE`, `BLOCKED_UPSTREAM_PHASE` and `_readiness_rows`), so the predecessor node in the build order creates nothing for §8 to narrow

findings.reason: an implementer following the named call gets plan-level data and cannot gate on sections, or silently reverts to the assembly §8 explicitly tells it to avoid, so the section must name the section-level reader it actually needs.
findings.text: "Each admission pass re-reads readiness ... It calls `_readiness_by_slug`" names a reader that returns one verdict per plan, `{str(row.get("slug")): str(row.get("readiness") or "unknown")}` (`reckon/crew/plan_review.py:3094-3124`), discarding the per-section data the same roadmap rows carry as `section_readiness` (`reckon/roadmap.py:3598`) and that §2's `_readiness_rows` reads; it therefore cannot answer whether an upstream *section* is declared done

findings.reason: recording the upstream's project when the wait is stored remains correct and still avoids depending on a deleted pointer, so the mechanism stands even though this justification overstates why.
findings.text: §8 states "A run's live pointer, the one record naming its project, is deleted when the run is promoted", but a promoted run's project is reconstructed from its surviving run directory (`_rebuild_record_from_run_directory`, `reckon/crew/promotion_records.py:77-105`, which derives `project` from the supervisor record), so the pointer is not the only record naming it

rubric_items.done_when: pass — the changed arms each assert a distinct refusal or transition with a declared negative arm: cross-project launch only after `B:plan#s2` is done; mutual-section cycle refused with both refs named and nothing stored; mixed section/`--after` cycle refused naming X and `A#s1`; `blocked`/`failed` closures move the waiter to `blocked-upstream` and never launch; a `complete`-but-unlanded upstream leaves its waiter `awaiting-upstream` and releases it on the pass after the ledger row appears.
